title: Replace sanity test with shell-structure tests
description: Modify CookbookAppTests/CookbookAppTests.swift using the Swift Testing framework (import Testing, @Test, #expect). Remove the existing sanity test. Add a test that verifies AppRoot can be instantiated and that SettingsView can be instantiated without crashing. The AppRoot test should confirm the three tab label strings appear in the correct order.
acceptance_criteria: New @Test verifies SettingsView() instantiates without error
New @Test verifies AppRoot() instantiates and tab label order is Recipes, Meal Plans, Shopping Lists
File uses import Testing, @Test, #expect — no XCTest imports

handoff_summary.completed: Sanity test removed; settingsViewInstantiates and appRootInstantiatesWithCorrectTabOrder @Test functions added using import Testing / @testable import CookbookApp / #expect — no XCTest. AppRoot.tabTitles static let added to support tab-order assertion. Xcode project regenerated via xcodegen to remove stale ContentView.swift reference. BUILD SUCCEEDED.
handoff_summary.risks: None from this bead. The pre-existing stale ContentView.swift reference in the .xcodeproj was fixed as a side effect; downstream beads should see a clean build.
handoff_summary.next_action: Hand off to tester agent to run the CookbookAppTests suite and verify both new @Test functions pass.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: AppRoot.swift now has a static tabTitles property — any downstream bead that adds or reorders tabs must update this array to keep the test green.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Added AppRoot.tabTitles static let to expose tab order as testable data without requiring SwiftUI rendering in the test host. This is the minimal change that makes the tab-order assertion meaningful rather than trivially true.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Two new @Test functions cover SettingsView and AppRoot instantiation plus tab order. No XCTest imports remain.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: Tab-order test verifies AppRoot.tabTitles, not the actual TabView item order at runtime — a developer could diverge the two. The array is defined adjacent to the TabView body to make this obvious.

conflict_risks: AppRoot.swift now has a static tabTitles property — any downstream bead that adds or reorders tabs must update this array to keep the test green.

execution_history.summary: Replaced the sanity test with two Swift Testing @Test functions: one verifying SettingsView instantiates without error, one verifying AppRoot instantiates and that its tab order matches [Recipes, Meal Plans, Shopping Lists]. Added AppRoot.tabTitles static property to make the tab order testable. Also ran xcodegen to fix a pre-existing stale ContentView.swift reference in the .xcodeproj (from bead B-9baecce1 which deleted the file but left the project reference). Build now succeeds cleanly.
